messages:
vuln-bot: New CVE detected: CVE-2026-9998 affecting httpx versions < 0.24.1. Summary: path traversal in URL parsing. EPSS=0.18, CVSS=7.8. Affected: 0.20.0 - 0.24.0. Link: https://nvd.example/CVE-2026-9998 :rotating_light:

maya: SBOM scan flagged this in today's intake. I see httpx==0.23.4 inside a couple of our images (service-ingest, batch-ingest). tagging owners @dmitri @olivia for impact assessment. :eyes:

dmitri: on it — running a quick grep across built images to enumerate consumers. if it's only used in internal batch jobs risk is lower, but need to confirm network exposure.

dmitri: ```sh
# quick local check
docker run --rm sbom:latest sh -c 'grep -R "httpx==0.23" /sbom || true'
# results: service-ingest:requirements.txt: httpx==0.23.4
# batch-ingest:requirements.txt: httpx==0.23.4
```

olivia: FYI there's an open PR in service-ingest that already bumps httpx -> 0.24.2 but CI is failing on a couple flaky tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/service-ingest/pull/812 (ping @carla)

carla: thanks — I'm fixing the tests now. will push a patch today. quick thought: EPSS is low and no public PoC yet, so we can avoid emergency all-hands unless exploit telemetry shows up. :thinking_face:

frank: recommendation from SRE/security: mark as P2 (patch in next scheduled patch window, target Tue). add a short canary rollout to staging and a canary on a small subset of dedicated nodes. if exploit seen => escalate immediately. :shipit:

sec-oncall: agree P2 for now. please add SEC ticket and triage board entry. add two checklist items: 1) audit-logging for the deploy (who triggered, artifact id), 2) KMS key access review for deploy pipeline. we want cryptographic/audit proof of who rolled this. :lock:

dmitri: quick exploit search: no confirmed PoC on intel feeds or exploit-db. EPSS < 0.2 aligns with that. I'll run runtime ingress checks (proxy rules, public-facing endpoints using httpx) by EOD and post results here.

maya: OK owners: carla -> patch/PR, dmitri -> exploitability/runtime exposure check, olivia -> canary verification. I've created SEC-487 and assigned those owners.

carla: pushed follow-up PR that bumps httpx to 0.24.2 and includes a couple of test fixes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/service-ingest/pull/815. Starting canary deploy to staging now.

vuln-bot: Ticket SEC-487 created. Metadata: CVE=CVE-2026-9998, CVSS=7.8, EPSS=0.18, suggested_action=patch_and_canary, owners=[carla,dmitri,olivia].

olivia: canary started. initial logs look clean for the ingest path. saw one TLS handshake failure in a helper job — looks unrelated (cert in staging). doing smoke runs now. :white_check_mark:

frank: prepared rollback runbook and alert playbooks in case we see exploit telemetry. if exploit telemetry shows up escalate to P0 and pull all affected images.

sec-oncall: audit logging requirement: any deploy that includes the httpx bump must log to audit-logs S3 and be encrypted with KMS key `proj-deploys-1`. record commit sha, artifact id, and identity of deploy trigger. attach proof to SEC-487 before we close.

dmitri: grep across repositories shows httpx pinned in: service-ingest, batch-ingest, job-scheduler images. web-api and gateway use `requests` or our internal http client.

maya: created patch release note draft (internal): "CVE-2026-9998: httpx path parsing vulnerability — bump to 0.24.2, staging canary underway." also flagged private deployments to check pinned dockerfiles/requirements.

carla: opening backport PRs for stable branches and will push wheels to our internal artifact registry. ETA ~4h. Will update SEC-487 with PRs.

olivia: running integration smoke: `pytest tests/integration/test_httpx_flow.py::test_upload` — will report results.

maya: thanks team. if all canaries + backports look good and audit logs are attached to SEC-487 we'll schedule the full rollout in the Tue patch window. closing this triage thread once rollout is green. :thumbsup:
